persona_name: High-income household that feels financially disorganized
problem_statement: Financially complex households with a mix of individual and shared accounts can struggle to maintain an accurate, shared, continuity-ready picture of accounts, bills, credentials, and key documents, leaving one person to reconstruct or hand over critical information.
search_demand_evidence: OBS-000113 and OBS-000119 explicitly seek a complete-view workflow; OBS-000126 seeks a mixed joint/separate configuration.
severity_evidence: Account visibility and continuity failures can delay review or leave a spouse unable to locate information; typical financial loss is unknown.
spending_evidence: OBS-000114, OBS-000125, and OBS-000135 report paid or active shared/aggregation app use.
spending_frequency: Reported monthly subscription or annual paid-app use; retention and target-persona prevalence are UNKNOWN.
time_currently_spent: Recurring manual review, spreadsheet updates, logins, and information handoff; no representative time total.
time_frequency: Monthly, annual, or event-driven, depending on the household.
trigger_event: Marriage, account growth, home purchase, a need to review finances, a change in household responsibility, or an unexpected absence of the primary financial operator.
urgency_evidence: The work becomes more consequential during handoff or absence, but immediate urgency is not established across the sample.
willingness_to_pay: WEAK to MODERATE at category level; no distinct-continuity willingness to pay established.
willingness_to_pay_evidence: Paid app use supports finance-tool category spend, not payment for a new shared-inventory or handoff product.
workaround: Manual logins, account/card spreadsheets, shared credentials or folders, periodic finance meetings, and consolidating accounts where possible.
workaround_cost: FACT: one record reports repeated logins prevented monthly review; another reports multiple sheets. Exact time/cost is mostly UNKNOWN.

money_currently_spent: MODERATE for professional service category; portal capability is firm-selected and DMM prices are unpublished. WEAK for a separate client-side document workflow.
notes: FACT: 4 supporting observations, 4 independent URLs, 2 source types (Reddit and forum). Tier 1=2; Tier 2=0; Tier 4=2. persona_name: High-income household that feels financially disorganized
problem_statement: Financially complex households can repeatedly spend time collecting, categorizing, locating, and rechecking account and financial documents before a professional handoff, while relying on spreadsheets, folders, and memory to confirm the information is complete.
search_demand_evidence: The records describe preparation and hiring behavior, not a direct search for a standalone document-handoff product.
severity_evidence: Reported preparation took six to ten hours in one case, and another record followed a missing form. Typical time or financial consequence is unknown.
spending_evidence: OBS-000121 reports about US$3,500 in CPA spend after compiling records; OBS-000122 reports US$1,500 after spreadsheet preparation.
spending_frequency: Per annual preparation or professional engagement; recurrence is not measured.

willingness_to_pay: WEAK for a distinct household document-handoff workflow; no separate paid job established.

current_solution_satisfaction: MEDIUM to HIGH: repository evidence includes workable shared docs/templates, cadence, spreadsheet, and 15Five use; broader satisfaction/prevalence is unknown.
description: WORKFLOW-LED early hypothesis. The evidence supports recurring follow-through work and occasional continuity failures, not a claim that first-time managers need new software or that any particular product is inadequate.

existing_solution: Shared documents, recurring templates, action-item tracking, calendars, spreadsheets, task/project tools, 15Five, Lattice, Fellow, Leapsome, AI meeting assistants, coaching, mentoring, and manager practice.
existing_solution_type: Manual/shared-record workflows, task systems, dedicated 1:1 and meeting software, HR/performance-management platforms, AI meeting assistants, and manager-development support.
frequency_evidence: OBS-000138 describes a missed 1:1 development commitment; OBS-000141 and OBS-000143 describe weekly, fortnightly, or periodic 1:1 notes, priorities, and action tracking; OBS-000147 describes manual Google Docs/calendar-note work; OBS-000150 describes a missed recurring 1:1; OBS-000155 and OBS-000159 describe ongoing structured 1:1/performance records. Exact prevalence and cadence are unknown.
job_to_be_done: When I am managing recurring one-on-ones and follow-up commitments for my direct reports, help me retain the relevant context and reliably carry actions forward so I do not overlook commitments or reconstruct prior discussions.
market_size_estimate: UNKNOWN: no defensible persona-specific estimate at clustering stage.
money_currently_spent: FACT: incumbent category pricing and use exist, including 15Five AI add-ons and Lattice company-level platform packages. UNKNOWN: spend by a first-time manager or employer specifically to solve residual commitment follow-through after existing tools/processes.
notes: FACT: 8 supporting observations, 7 independent URLs, 3 source types (Reddit, Hacker News, App Store). Tier 1=1; Tier 2=0; Tier 4=7. Persona fit: HIGH=2 (OBS-000138, OBS-000147); MEDIUM=4 (OBS-000141, OBS-000143, OBS-000150, OBS-000155); LOW=2 (OBS-000156, OBS-000159). No SOURCE DIVERSITY GAP: three source types support this early hypothesis, although Reddit accounts for five supporting observations and Hacker News/App Store provide only one each. COUNTEREVIDENCE: shared documents/templates and action tracking work for some managers (OBS-000141); periodic 1:1 cadence can be adequate (OBS-000143); 15Five is described as useful for newer managers (OBS-000155); and a spreadsheet worked for performance clarity (OBS-000159). OBS-000156 is product-specific friction with LOW to MEDIUM persona fit. The evidence does not establish that the job persists beyond ordinary learning, that existing management practice or software fails broadly, or that a distinct paid job exists. MARKET ANALYST 2026-09-08: COMP-0026 (15Five) directly supports agendas, carried-forward actions, notes, check-ins, and AI-generated summaries/actions; COMP-0027 (Lattice) bundles 1:1s, updates, feedback, and performance/goals workflows into company-paid people software; COMP-0028 (Fellow) supplies a free shared 1:1/notes workflow plus action organization and paid AI/integrations; COMP-0029 (Leapsome) documents shared agendas, action ownership/history, goal/feedback links, and AI meeting memory. FACT: these capabilities materially cover the claimed mechanical residual. Repository counterevidence also shows shared docs/templates (OBS-000141), ordinary cadence (OBS-000143), 15Five adequacy (OBS-000155), and a spreadsheet (OBS-000159). OBS-000156 is one product-specific friction report, not proof of category-wide residual failure. CONCLUSION: NO distinct residual paid job is supported at this time. The remaining risk is primarily manager discipline, contextual judgment, organizational enablement, or adoption/integration quality; evidence of a separate buyer, payer, or willingness to pay after competent use is absent. See research/market-research/PROB-0014-market-analysis.md.
persona_name: New manager leading people for the first time
problem_statement: New people managers can struggle to maintain reliable follow-through on recurring one-on-one commitments, development actions, and performance context across direct reports, relying on memory and a mix of notes, calendars, templates, spreadsheets, or management tools.
search_demand: MODERATE for advice/process; WEAK for a separate residual product.
search_demand_evidence: OBS-000138 and OBS-000147 seek ways to retain context or make 1:1s productive. The reviewed sources do not show buyers searching for an additional layer after using credible manager, meeting, or HR platforms.
severity_evidence: OBS-000138 describes a month-long missed development commitment and OBS-000147 reports manual preparation/notes work. The sample does not establish representative economic, retention, or performance consequences.
spending_evidence: 15Five and Lattice official pricing pages checked 2026-09-08; OBS-000147, OBS-000155, OBS-000156. Category pricing/use must not be interpreted as residual-job willingness to pay.
time_currently_spent: Manual preparation, note retention, and action carry-forward are reported; no representative time total.
time_frequency: Weekly, fortnightly, or periodic 1:1 cycles in the supporting accounts; exact cadence varies.
trigger_event: A recurring one-on-one, a newly made development or performance commitment, a missed meeting, or a need to prepare for follow-up with a direct report.
urgency_evidence: The need becomes salient before a recurring 1:1 or after a missed commitment, but the evidence does not establish uniform immediate urgency.
willingness_to_pay: WEAK / NOT ESTABLISHED for a distinct residual follow-through job.
willingness_to_pay_evidence: FACT: 15Five lists AI add-ons at US$2 per employee/month and US$19 per manager/month, and Lattice lists company-paid performance/manager-tool packages from US$10 per seat/month with a US$4,000 annual minimum. These are category/platform prices. OBS-000147 and OBS-000155–000156 report tool use, not buyer/payer choice or payment for an additional residual layer. No direct switching, procurement, or separate payment evidence was found.
workaround: Use shared documents, recurring templates, calendar notes, action lists, spreadsheets, periodic 1:1s, or a dedicated management platform.
workaround_cost: FACT: OBS-000138 reports a commitment slipping for about a month; OBS-000147 reports manual Google Docs/calendar-note work; OBS-000156 reports manual retyping in one product. Representative time or financial cost is UNKNOWN.
